text:
Dylan Strome is doing the Dylan Strome things: 16 points in 18 games, 13 of them assists, at 3.05 points per 60, well above his talent range. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 98th percentile among forwards for primary shot assists last season, and that is still what he is in Washington's lineup.

The goals are the odd part. He has three on 5.8 expected (the quality of his chances), shooting 7.5%, and both of his goals in the last ten games came in one night against Buffalo on Oct. 24. His own chances are up to 1.11 expected goals per 60 from 0.78 last season, so our numbers call him due rather than declining. The Capitals have also scored 4.2 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice.

The usual caveat applies at the other end: Evolving-Hockey had opponents creating more with him on the ice last season (bottom 4% of forwards), and he is not quick, with a top speed in the 5th percentile. After back-to-back losses to New Jersey, including a 7-4 game, Washington could use the goals his chances say are coming.
headline: Dylan Strome is setting the table, not finishing
